query:
The group has a norm that plans are confirmed in the chat before being assumed to be happening. Which member does not follow this norm in practice, and what specific pattern of behaviour in the conversations shows they treat it as inapplicable to themselves?

Options:
A. Seb
B. Marcus
C. Priyanka
D. Zara
context:
[1] (about=Zara, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:44:00) You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.
[2] (about=Zara, episodic, t6 @2026-01-29T19:49:00) We are not annoyed at you. We just want to know in advance so we can plan accordingly. That is not too much to ask.
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:48:00) 70% is fine for standing. Don't do anything stupid like suddenly sprinting for a clue 😅
[4] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-02-19T20:03:00) You have been a vague maybe at every single plan since October. We all know what has been going on with you. The group misses you being properly here. Saturday was the first time in months you've actually shown up without hedging.
[5] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priyanka, group-interaction, t10 @2026-02-12T19:41:00) Escape room confirmed for Saturday 2pm.
[6] (about=GROUP, said_by=Seb, group-interaction, t0 @2026-01-08T19:14:00) Group tentatively agrees to meet Sunday evening for dinner, pending venue details.
[7] (about=Theo, episodic, t14 @2026-02-26T19:40:00) we met because Marcus accidentally walked into the wrong A&E bay and Nadia was the one who had to redirect him. you're right, camping is conservative
agent_answer:
A. Seb.

The specific behaviour is captured in Zara’s remark to him:  
“You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.”

This shows Seb expects others to confirm plans in advance, but when he is the one making/initiating the plan, he does not ask for confirmation himself — treating the norm as applying to everyone except him.

query:
The group has a stated norm that the role of booking and organising rotates — it does not fall to the same person every time. Which members are not following this norm in practice, and what in the conversations reveals their non-compliance?

Options:
A. Nadia and Theo
B. Seb and Marcus
C. Priyanka and Seb
D. Zara and Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Zara, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:41:00) I am done making all the reservations. I have done it for every single outing this month. Someone else can do it.
[2] (about=Zara, episodic, t10 @2026-02-12T19:44:00) You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priyanka, group-interaction, t6 @2026-01-29T19:23:00) Group considers escape room near Waterloo as alternative for Feb 14; Priyanka will look into booking.
[4] (about=Seb, episodic, t9 @2026-02-12T19:40:00) lads who's sorting the escape room booking for Saturday
[5] (about=Zara, episodic, t8 @2026-02-05T19:33:00) Three, but yes. The booking logistics alone are not worth it for a Tuesday-in-January mood.
agent_answer:
**Answer: B. Seb and Marcus**

- **Seb** — Seb asks *“lads who’s sorting the escape room booking for Saturday?”* instead of doing it himself. Zara calls this out directly: *“You do not ask when you are the one doing it, Seb. That is somewhat the point.”* So Seb is not taking his turn in the rotation.
- **Marcus** — The memory slice gives **no record** of Marcus ever doing any booking/organising, and Zara says she has made *“all the reservations… for every single outing this month.”* That shows the booking role has been falling to the same person and Marcus has not been taking his share of the rotation.

So the members not following the rotation norm are **Seb and Marcus**.
